question: Can workflow design for LLM tasks be automated end to end by searching over code-represented workflows with MCTS, beating hand-designed and prior automated workflows?
hypothesis: Tree-structured experience, execution feedback and soft-mixed selection let an LLM optimizer search the workflow space more efficiently than ADAS's linear history.
contributions: Formalise workflow optimisation as search over nodes and edges, generalising prior approaches
AFLOW: MCTS-based method with operators, discovering workflows with minimal human intervention
Evaluation on six benchmarks: +5.7% over manual methods, +19.5% over automated approaches, smaller models beating larger ones on cost-performance

method.summary: AFLOW treats an agentic workflow as code (LLM-invoking nodes with prompt parameters, edges as Python control flow, plus predefined operators) and searches over whole workflows with an MCTS variant. An optimizer LLM (Claude-3.5-sonnet) makes one modification per round from the selected workflow's tree-structured experience (success and failure children, plus execution logs), each candidate is executed five times on a validation set, and results are backpropagated. Evaluated on six benchmarks against hand-designed methods and ADAS.

results.claim: AFLOW averages 80.3% across six benchmarks with GPT-4o-mini as executor.
results.setup: Table 1; HotpotQA/DROP F1, HumanEval/MBPP pass@1, GSM8K/MATH solve rate; GPT-4o-mini executor, Claude-3.5-sonnet optimizer, 20 rounds; test split, mean of three runs; best manual baseline CoT SC avg 76.0

results.claim: AFLOW beats manual methods by 5.7% on average and automated optimisation (ADAS) by 19.5%.
results.note: Paper does not say whether 5.7 and 19.5 are relative or absolute; averages in Table 1 are 80.3 vs 76.0 (CoT SC) and 67.2 (ADAS).
results.quote: Workflows optimized by AFLOW outperform all manually designed methods by an average of 5.7% and surpass contemporary automatic workflow optimization work by 19.5%.

results.claim: ADAS scores below plain IO on average, so a naive linear-history search can lose to no workflow at all.
results.setup: Table 1, ADAS run with Claude-3.5-sonnet optimizer, GPT-4o-mini executor, 30 rounds; IO baseline 72.8

results.claim: AFLOW improves over ADAS on MATH level 5 and MBPP by about 57%.
results.note: MBPP 83.4 vs 53.4 and MATH 56.2 vs 35.4 in Table 1.
results.quote: improving over ADAS on MATHlv5∗and MBPP tasks by 57%
